subject: Critical dependency patch and optional rollback window — immediate customer guidance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmeops.com>; acme-sre@acme.com
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Critical dependency patch and optional rollback window — immediate customer guidance

Hi Alice / Acme SRE team,

Short version: we discovered a critical bug in a shared C++ runtime dependency that under rare high-concurrency conditions can cause tokenization mismatches and increased memory growth for long-running sessions. The runtime team is rolling a targeted patch and we need to apply it across active inference clusters in your region this morning.

Planned action (short notice):
- Start: 2028-03-01 08:55 PT (in ~43 minutes)
- Expected per-host window: 5–12 minutes (rolling, staggered)
- Global finish target: by 2028-03-01 09:30 PT

What we need from you:
- If you have any scheduled large-batch generation jobs starting between 09:00–10:30 PT, please pause or reschedule them until we confirm completion.
- If you run long-running sessions pinned to a single worker, please notify acme-sre@acme.com immediately if those sessions are critical; we can prioritize non-disruptive host scheduling for them.

Risk and mitigation highlights:
- Impact: transient dropped tokens and rare session restarts under sustained concurrency — we have not observed data exfiltration or model corruption.
- Mitigation: rolling patch with KV-cache integrity checks, automatic health checks, and a fast rollback path if we see regression.

Attachments: short summary of the patch and a checklist (see attached).

We realize this is short notice — apologies. Our priority is to prevent a wider surface failure; we will push a follow-up within 30 minutes with a live progress update and a concrete completion time.

If you want a quick sync phone call, I’m available now — reply with a number.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: dependency-patch-summary.pdf; rollout-checklist.md

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmeops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-sre@acme.com
Date: 2028-03-01T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Critical dependency patch and optional rollback window — immediate customer guidance

Thanks Marissa — we saw this and are coordinating internally. Quick questions:

1) Can you confirm whether currently active inference sessions will be terminated or paused? We have a nightly reconciliation job that keeps warm sessions pinned and it runs at 09:15 PT.
2) If rollback is needed, what is the expected time to restore the pre-patch state?

We’ll hold the 09:15 job for now but need to understand the window.

—Alice
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Payment Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Critical dependency patch and optional rollback window — immediate customer guidance

Internal notes / action items:

Quoted original to keep context.

Stephanie / runtime: please confirm the behavior for pinned long-running sessions — we need exact wording for customer. Rishi, prepare the rollback play: how quickly can we revert and reassign sessions without data loss? Ben, please stand by to coordinate customer comms and confirm the series of health-check metrics we’ll publish to the status page.

Rollback constraints we discussed earlier:
- Fast rollback available but requires draining in-flight KV-cache writes; estimate 8–12 minutes per host to rehydrate state.
- If we must rollback, we should pause scheduling to that pool and route traffic to an unaffected pool in the same region.

Also: enable verbose telemetry for the patch window (trace-id prefix: acme-20280301) and capture a sample of tokenization diffs for first 50 requests after patch.

Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmeops.com>; acme-sre@acme.com
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Critical dependency patch and optional rollback window — immediate customer guidance

Hi Alice — quick update: patching completed at 12:18 PT, rollout finished across your regional clusters. Summary:

- Total hosts patched: 48 (rolling, staggered)
- Observed customer-facing impact: 3 short-lived session restarts (automatically recovered), no tokenization divergence reported beyond the transient cases we mitigated.
- Rollback not required; we held the rollback window until 12:30 PT and did not trigger.

Action items for Acme:
- Please resume scheduled jobs at your convenience. If you see any unexpected tokenization or model-output shifts, reply with a sample payload and the trace-id (we captured samples under trace prefix "acme-20280301").
- We attached the post-deploy checklist and the patch summary for your compliance/audit team.

Attachments: rollout-checklist.md, dependency-patch-summary.pdf

Thanks for your patience. If you’d like a short postmortem call this week to walk through telemetry and the regression safeguards, I can schedule with Stephanie and Rishi.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: rollout-checklist.md; dependency-patch-summary.pdf
